{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=2740
#   --ntasks=16
#   --nodes=1
#   --cpus-per-task=1
#   --mem-per-cpu=1000mb
#   -t 6:00:00
#   --qos=hennig
#   --ntasks-per-socket=16
#   --ntasks-per-node=16
#   -o out_%j.log
#   -e err_%j.log

#flux: --job-name=2740
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 16
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=6h

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu=1000mb
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --qos=hennig
# Flux QoS/priority mappings are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may have different priority/limits than intended, affecting wait time or eligibility.

# Omitted Slurm options: --ntasks-per-socket=16 and --ntasks-per-node=16
# Flux does not have a universally portable directive for these placement constraints.
# Performance implication: rank placement/NUMA locality may differ, potentially reducing performance.

# Omitted Slurm options: -o/-e with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

# Slurm variable $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR is not set under Flux.
cd "${FLUX_JOB_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}"

module purge
module load intel/2019.1.144
module load openmpi/4.0.1

# Slurm used srun --mpi=pmix_v3; under Flux, use flux-run.
# Performance implication: if your MPI build requires a specific PMI/PMIx selection, site-specific settings may be needed.
flux run -n 16 -c 1 /home/joshuapaul/vasp_10-23-19_5.4.4/bin/vasp_stand > job.log

echo Done
"
}
